title: Illinois's 14th Congressional District election, 2026
description: The election for Illinois's 14th Congressional District pits four-term Democratic incumbent Lauren Underwood against Republican challenger James Marter in a rematch of their 2024 contest. The district covers the outer western and northern suburbs of Chicago, including Naperville, DeKalb, Joliet, and Oswego, and was significantly redrawn after the 2020 Census to be more Democratic-leaning. Underwood, first elected in 2018 by flipping the seat, has become a national Democratic figure as co-chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee and a leader on maternal health policy. Marter, a conservative activist and former Kendall County Republican chairman, is making his fourth consecutive bid for this seat and has centered his campaign on reducing federal spending, securing the border, and opposing abortion rights.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for the 2026 general election in Illinois's 14th Congressional District as of mid-June 2026.

candidates.name: Lauren Underwood
candidates.summary: Lauren Underwood is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois's 14th Congressional District, first elected in 2018. A registered nurse and public health professional, she served as a senior advisor at the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services under the Obama administration and is co-chair of the House Democratic Policy and Communications Committee. She is a leading voice on maternal health, co-founding the Black Maternal Health Caucus, and serves on the House Appropriations Committee.

candidates.name: James Marter
candidates.summary: James 'Jim' Marter is a Republican candidate for U.S. House in Illinois's 14th Congressional District, making his fourth consecutive bid for the seat. A former Kendall County Republican Chairman and deputy on the Illinois 14th District Republican State Central Committee, he also serves as an Oswego Library District Board Trustee. Marter runs as a conservative focused on reducing federal spending, border security, repealing the Affordable Care Act, and protecting Second Amendment rights.

forecast.rationale: No public 2026 general-election polls exist for this race, so the forecast relies on structural non-polling indicators. Lauren Underwood is a four-term Democratic incumbent in a district that was significantly redrawn after the 2020 Census to be more Democratic-leaning. The challenger, James Marter, is making his fourth consecutive bid for this seat without having won previously. These factors — incumbency, a favorable district map, and a repeat challenger — point to a clear Democratic advantage. However, the complete absence of voter polling, combined with the midterm-election environment (typically challenging for the incumbent president's party), introduces meaningful uncertainty, warranting medium confidence rather than high.
